en.headline: Transport Department warns public of fake Toyota airbag recall messages
en.dek: Officials said the department does not send individual recall letters to owners and has referred the fraudulent WhatsApp notices to police.
body: The Transport Department has alerted the public to fraudulent vehicle airbag safety recall messages circulating on WhatsApp that falsely claim to come from the department and concern Toyota vehicles.

A spokesman said the department has no connection with the letters or messages that make unauthorised use of its name. At present it only lists safety recall information provided by authorised dealers of registered vehicle manufacturers on its official website and does not issue letters to individual owners.

The department urged residents not to provide any personal information in response to unofficial messages purportedly from the government and said the case has been referred to police for follow-up. Anyone who has already supplied details should contact the police.
Vehicle owners were advised to verify any recall information directly with the relevant authorised agents or dealers and to remain alert to messages from unknown sources.

zh.headline: 運輸署呼籲提防偽冒豐田安全氣袋召回信息
zh.dek: 署方表示不會以信件通知個別車主召回事宜，並已將有關偽冒WhatsApp信息轉交警方跟進。
body: 運輸署今日呼籲市民提高警覺，提防偽冒署方名義、涉及豐田汽車安全氣袋召回的信息在WhatsApp廣泛流傳。
發言人澄清，署方與未經授權使用部門名稱的偽冒信件或信息沒有任何關係。目前署方只會在官方網頁列出由註冊車輛製造商授權香港代理提供的召回資訊，不會發信通知個別車主。
署方促請市民切勿誤信非官方途徑訛稱為政府的信息，或提供任何個人資料，事件已轉交警方跟進。曾因偽冒信息提供個人資料的人士應盡快聯絡警方。
車主如有疑問，應直接與有關授權代理或經銷商查詢，並對不明來歷的信息保持警惕。
